import math
import statistics

# National Defense expenditures (in millions of dollars)
expenditures = {
    1933: 680,
    1934: 531,
    1935: 689,
    1936: 900,
    1937: 929,
    1938: 1029,
    1939: 1206,
    1940: 1657,
    1941: 6301  # includes urgent ship construction (emergency ship construction from March 1941)
}

# Calculate year-to-year log growth rates
years = sorted(expenditures.keys())
log_growth_rates = []
for i in range(1, len(years)):
    prev_year = years[i-1]
    curr_year = years[i]
    ratio = expenditures[curr_year] / expenditures[prev_year]
    log_growth = math.log(ratio)
    log_growth_rates.append(log_growth)
    print(f"{prev_year}->{curr_year}: {expenditures[prev_year]} -> {expenditures[curr_year]}, ratio = {ratio:.4f}, log growth = {log_growth:.4f}")

print(f"\nLog growth rates: {log_growth_rates}")

# Calculate coefficient of variation using population standard deviation
mean = sum(log_growth_rates) / len(log_growth_rates)
variance = sum((x - mean) ** 2 for x in log_growth_rates) / len(log_growth_rates)  # population variance
std_dev = math.sqrt(variance)  # population standard deviation
cv = std_dev / mean  # coefficient of variation

print(f"\nMean: {mean:.4f}")
print(f"Population Std Dev: {std_dev:.4f}")
print(f"Coefficient of Variation: {cv:.4f}")
print(f"Rounded to nearest hundredth: {round(cv, 2)}")
